entities.summary: Jacobus de Cessolis was an Italian author of the most famous morality book on chess in the Middle Ages. Born in the early 13th century, de Cessolis was a member of the nobility and received a humanist education, which influenced his writing. His book, 'De Casibus Virorum Illustrium', became a foundational text for medieval moral education and was widely read in Europe. De Cessolis's work not only reflected the societal values of his time but also contributed to the development of a more nuanced understanding of human nature and the consequences of one's actions. This legacy can be seen in the continued study and adaptation of his ideas in modern chess and philosophy. The book's enduring influence is a testament to de Cessolis's skill as a writer and thinker, and his work remains an important part of the cultural heritage of medieval Italy.
